g.text: Dispatch via AllToAll in MoE inference
A critical component of distributed MoE inference is the dispatch phase,
where tokens are redistributed across GPUs via AllToAll collective
communication to reach their assigned experts (Hwang et al., 2022;
g.title: N4 [Context] (cites=2) A critical component of distributed MoE inference is the dispatch phase, where tokens are redistributed across GPUs via AllToAll collective communication to reach their assigned experts (Hwang et al., 2022; Rajbhandari et al., 2022).

g.title: N5 [Prior_Work] (cites=0) CUDA graphs have become essential for high-throughput inference, as they eliminate kernel launch overhead by capturing and replaying sequences of GPU operations.

g.text: However, CUDA graphs require all buffer sizes to be fixed at capture time,

current approaches must allocate buffers for the worst-case token count
g.title: N6 [Limitation] (cites=0) However, CUDA graphs require all buffer sizes to be fixed at capture time, creating a fundamental tension with the dynamic nature of MoE routing: current approaches must allocate buffers for the worst-case token count across all peer pairs, leading to substantial padding waste.

g.title: N7 [Result] (cites=0) Our analysis of Mixtral-8x7B routing traces reveals that this worst-case allocation is highly inefficient.

g.title: N8 [Result] (cites=0) The maximum per-peer token count (Cmax = 43) is 8.4× larger than the mean count (5.1), resulting in 88% padding overhead.

g.title: N9 [Result] (cites=0) However, the distribution is heavy-tailed: 99% of per-peer counts fall below C = 16, suggesting that smaller buffers could handle the vast majority of dispatch operations.

g.text: We propose Cap-and-Spill, a two-pass dispatch strategy that exploits this

g.title: N11 [Method] (cites=0) The first pass uses quantile-based buffer capacity (C = Q99 ) to handle most tokens efficiently; the second pass dispatches overflow tokens that exceed the capacity.

g.title: C1 [Contribution] (cites=0) We propose Cap-and-Spill, a two-pass CUDA-graph-compatible MoE dispatch algorithm that uses quantile-based buffer capacity to reduce padding waste while handling overflow tokens in a second pass.

g.title: C2 [Contribution] (cites=0) We demonstrate 33.9% mean latency reduction (1077 µs → 712 µs) on 8×A100 NVLink with Mixtral-8x7B routing traces, recovering 53.2% of the gap to oracle eager dispatch while maintaining exact correctness.

g.title: C3 [Contribution] (cites=0) We characterize the heavy-tailed nature of MoE routing distributions (Cmax /µ = 8.4×) and show that the 99th percentile provides the optimal operating point, balancing buffer reduction (2.69×) with minimal overflow (5.4%).
